title: Latency Threading Snapshot — Weekly Communique
body:
Weekly Snapshot: Latency Threading and Batching — Summary (2028-11-03 to 2028-11-10)

Attendees: Asha (chairs), Diego, Claire, Jun, Ravi, oncall: Maya
Absentees: N/A

One-line: Focus this week on threading model changes for the kernel scheduler, a KV-cache shadow experiment across two regions, and a safe micro-batching fallback to tighten P95 tail under bursty short queries.

Agenda/Notes
- Kernel threading update (Jun):
  - RFC merged into staging (PR 4521). Scheduler now exposes a per-worker affinity hint for I/O-bound prefill tasks vs CPU-bound token-gen tasks.
  - Measured on dev-cluster: token-generation throughput unchanged, but cold-start P95 improved by ~18% for sequences <=128 tokens when prefill tasks are pinned off GPU-worker threads.
  - Open concern: starvation observed on a node with heavy KV-prefill when pod-level cgroups are enabled — caused by thread pool max of 48. Action: reduce default max to 32 for next canary.

- KV-cache shadowing (Diego):
  - Shadow run across us-east-1 and eu-west-1 for 48 hours capturing prefix hit/miss and end-to-end latency.
  - Key results: global hit ratio increased from 62% -> 71% for the sampled workload after enabling LRU window extension (config: window_ms=350).
  - Latency breakdown: median retrieval time from cache: 1.8ms (us-east), 2.4ms (eu-west). Miss penalty (cold fetch) median: 7.6ms.
  - Regression risk flagged: occasional 12–18ms spikes correlated with GC cycles in the Python-side cache coordinator. Proposal: port coordinator hotspot to Rust microservice (spike PR sketched).

- Batching and micro-batching fallback (Claire):
  - New micro-batcher heuristics: max-delay-ms lowered to 10ms for short-query cohort (token_len<=64). This tightened P50/P95 but increased server-side batching rate by ~6%.
  - Canary observed a 9% CPU increase; trade-off acceptable for hosted tier but not for Dedicate-small. Plan: gate on customer tier and allow config override.

- Prefill coalescer experiments (Ravi):
  - Coalescer delta strategy (group by prompt hash prefix) tested. Reduced duplicate prefill rate by 31% across sampled traffic.
  - Edge case: prompts with dynamic system tokens break grouping—added guard to drop grouping when system token entropy > threshold.

Operational metrics snapshot (week-over-week):
- P50 generation latency (short queries <=64): 42ms -> 36ms (improvement)
- P95 generation latency (short queries <=64): 198ms -> 162ms (improvement)
- KV-cache global hit-rate: 62% -> 71% (shadow run)
- Average tokens/sec per GPU during peak: 72k -> 68k (slight drop due to micro-batcher config)
- Error spikes: no new 5xx trend; two incidents labeled INF-ops-220 and INF-ops-221 (both transient prefill timeouts)

Decisions made
- Rollout schedule:
  - Week 0 (canary): kernel-thread affinity with pool max=32 on 5% of traffic (us-east-1).
  - Week 1: expand to 25% if no regression in GC-linked latency spikes.
  - Week 2: enable micro-batcher short-query profile for hosted only; do not enable for Dedicated-small until payload CPU delta resolved.
- KV-cache coordinator: start a Tech Spike to prototype Rust coordinator. If prototype reduces service GC pauses in synthetic tests by >=75%, schedule migration Q1 2029.

Action items (owners and due dates)
- Jun: push canary change to us-east-1 with pool max=32 and monitoring hooks (SLO dashboards) — due 2028-11-06
- Diego: run extended KV shadow with coordinator sampling enabled to capture allocation profiles — due 2028-11-09
- Claire: tune micro-batcher CPU guard and implement tier gate for Dedicated-small — due 2028-11-08
- Ravi: add entropy guard for prefill coalescer and deploy to staging — due 2028-11-05
- Maya (oncall): add automated alert that fires on sustained prefill miss-rate delta >10% over 5 minutes — due 2028-11-07

Risks and blockers
- GC-induced latency spikes from Python coordinator could undermine latency wins; prototype risk and timeline unknown.
- Dedicated-small customers may see CPU cost regressions; must provide opt-out flag and clear rollout docs.
- Threading affinity might expose hidden race conditions under heavy eviction churn — testing needed in stress harness.

Notes for product/console integration
- Add a new toggle in Console: "Short-query micro-batching (hosted)" with explanation of CPU vs latency tradeoffs and a per-route override in rollout policies.
- Add a dashboard card showing "KV shadow delta: hit-rate vs production" to let SRE teams monitor experiments in region.

Follow-up meeting: Fri 2028-11-10 09:30 PT — focus on canary telemetry and initial Rust spike proposal.

Appendix: experiment artifacts and quick links
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4521 (kernel threading affinity)
- Draft spike: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4603 (kv-coordinator-rust-prototype sketch)
- JIRA tickets referenced: JIRA-INF-7823 (kv-shadowing), JIRA-INF-7934 (micro-batcher-tiering), JIRA-INF-7951 (kernel-starvation)

Loose brainstorming notes (notes-to-self style)
- Could we leverage a tiny pinned core set for coordinator RPCs to avoid GC coupling?
- Consider an adaptive micro-batching that backs off during CPU saturation windows (signal from node-exporter).
- If Rust coordinator looks promising, evaluate memory footprint vs Python baseline and cold-start tradeoffs.

End of communique.
